prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you have referred to the Fourth of July as 'the holidays.' Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts collar, leans into microphone*

Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the committee, I appear before you today voluntarily and with a clear conscience.

I categorically deny the charge. I have never, at any cookout, potluck, or lake house gathering, referred to the Fourth of July as "the holidays." I know what "the holidays" means, Mr. Chairman. It means December. It means eggnog. It does not mean the Fourth.

I wish to state for the record: I say "the Fourth." Sometimes "the Fourth of July" in full, when speaking formally. On occasion, "Independence Day," when feeling patriotic or addressing my grandmother.

Now, the committee has entered into evidence a text message from July 2nd of last year reading, quote, "see you at the thing this weekend." I will address this directly. "The thing" referred to Gary's cookout. Gary's cookout WAS a Fourth of July celebration. Calling it "the thing" was casual, perhaps regrettably informal — but it was not, I repeat NOT, a de-Americanization of the holiday. Singular. Holiday, singular.

Am I now, or have I ever been, a person who brings a quinoa salad to a barbecue? I plead the Fifth on that, Mr. Chairman. But on the central charge, I am innocent.

I brought burgers. I brought sparklers. I stood for the fireworks even though my knee was acting up.

I have named no one. I have nothing further. God bless America, and God bless Gary's above-ground pool.
